Join the City of Chattanooga Team Chattanooga , a vibrant and growing community of over 190,000 residents within a metropolitan area of nearly 600,000 is known as the "Scenic City" for a reason. Nestled along the Tennessee River and surrounded by the foothills of the Appalachian Mountains, we are a hub of outdoor adventure and innovation. Home to the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga (UTC) and Chattanooga State Community College , our city blends a rich industrial history with a tech-forward future—famously powered by the nation’s first community-wide "Gig" fiber-optic network.​ The City of Chattanooga was also recently designated as a "National Park City,” the first of its kind in the United States. Our Organization As a City, we are powered by a dedicated workforce of approximately ​ 2,600 employees committed to excellence in public service and making Chattanooga the best community in the country. Our team ensures our city thrives through a wide range of municipal services, including: Public Safety: Chattanooga Police and Fire Departments. Infrastructure Utilities: Public Works, Waste Resources, and specialized Stormwater management. Quality of Life: Award-winning Parks and Outdoors and Community Development systems and the Chattanooga Public Library. Transportation: The Chattanooga Metropolitan Airport (CHA) and citywide transit and pedestrian friendly initiatives. Innovation: Leading-edge smart-city programs with a commitment to cutting edge workforce development policies to ensure all our residents can get ahead. Why Choose Chattanooga? The City of Chattanooga’s workforce is the heartbeat of our community. We don't just offer jobs; we offer careers with purpose: making Chattanooga the best city in America. We are committed to being the premier employer of choice in Southeast Tennessee by providing: Competitive Compensation: Robust pay scales that reflect our commitment to our staff. Work-Life Balance: Generous paid time off and flexible scheduling where possible. Exceptional Wellness: Comprehensive health benefits and wellness programs designed for you and your family that deliver savings to you beyond your paycheck, featuring a centralized health clinic and pharmacy for all City employees. . Growth: A focus on professional development and upward mobility within the organization. ​The Great Outdoors: Your Backyard Playground: Chattanooga isn't just near nature, it's immersed in it. As one of the most biodiverse cities in North America, the "Scenic City" offers an ecological richness that few places on earth can claim. Whether you are an adrenaline junkie or a weekend wanderer, world-class adventure is always less than an hour away. ​Vertical Adventures: Scale legendary sandstone cliffs in what is widely considered the premier rock climbing hub of the Southeast. Water Rapids: From the high-octane whitewater kayaking of the Ocoee River to world-class bass fishing and peaceful paddling on the Tennessee River. Trails for Miles: Explore a massive network of mountain biking and hiking trails that wind through lush ridges, hidden waterfalls, and deep river gorges. In Chattanooga, "work-life balance" means you can finish your shift and be at a trailhead or on the water before the sun sets. Our mission is to work together to build a safe, vibrant, and sustainable city for all Chattanoogans. To do that, it takes a team of skilled and passionate individuals. So, if you’d like to call Chattanooga home – or maybe you already do! – and want to further your career through meaningful work that makes a true impact where you live, we’d love to talk to you. Oversees monitoring of data quality and identifies methods for improving the quality of data being published. Supports third-party intermediaries wishing to access data and makes data accessible to different users through tools and applications. Conducts operational data reviews to evaluate business processes, analyze root causes, improve data quality, and monitor service delivery metrics. Facilitates the impactful use of open data by collaborating with communities and ensuring all data added to the open data portal is useful, usable, and accessible. Must meet regular attendance requirements. Must be able to maintain good interpersonal relationships with staff, co-workers, managers, and citizens. Proficient with Jira, Bitbucket (version control), and Confluence for documentation, tracking tasks, managing repositories, and driving agile projects. Knowledge of professional collection development principles; programming languages; creative problem-solving; and open data concepts. Hands-on experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP), BigQuery, Python (or similar scripting languages), SQL, Dataform, and Web API, or ability to learn quickly. Experience with Airbyte Airflow or similar, Cloud Run, Gemini Enterprise, ADK, and/or Gemini Enterprise Agent platform is preferred. Experience using and developing generative AI workflows (e.g., Google Gemini, LLMs, prompt engineering) to streamline analytics pipelines and workplace efficiency. Ability to research and provide formal analyses and recommendations. Ability to analyze data to evaluate effectiveness and make recommendations based upon insights. Ability to understand both qualitative and quantitative aspects of data and performance measurement. Works collaboratively and maintains positive interdepartmental partnerships. Demonstrated capacity for innovation, self-motivation, self-learning, self- learning and goal achievement; Strong critical and creative thinking skills to assess and resolve problems or issues by gathering and assessing information and using independent, professional judgment. Skilled in working with a variety of internal and external stakeholders. Skilled in effective written and oral communications that articulate complex information and issues clearly and simply. Skilled in gaining insight from quantitative and qualitative data. PHYSICAL DEMANDS: Positions in this class typically require fingering, grasping, talking, hearing, seeing, and repetitive motions. The Moccasin Bend Roll & Stroll is next Saturday, 9/26! 🎉  This event is organized by Chattanooga's Parks and Outdoors with Outdoor Chattanooga, with a ribbon-cutting at 10 Hamm Road (the NPS Gateway Site) and popsicles to be provided afterward at Renaissance Park.  Celebrate the addition of another 1.2-miles of greenway to the City's network, providing federal lands connectivity to the Moccasin Bend National Archaeological Site from nearby North Chattanooga. The project highlights the intersection of street safety and public space connections that stem from RPA's 2012 Moccasin Bend Gateway Plan, from the shared-use sidepath being added to the road diet it required along Manufacturers Road and Hamm Road, along with low impact development design strategies, and native plantings that frame the pathway.  Join neighbors, families, and outdoor enthusiasts to celebrate more than 10 years of partnerships toward the project between City Departments of Planning, Public Works, and Parks and Outdoors. The ribbon-cutting will be followed by a community trek down the brand-new, safely protected trail straight into Renaissance Park.

Chattajack Volunteers Needed :) —Help Bring Chattajack Village to Life! The vision for our new finish experience at River Gorge Ranch began nearly two years ago. Now, after months of planning and preparation, we need an incredible volunteer crew to help bring it to life on race day! So far, 26 volunteers have stepped forward to support our finish operations—19 at River Gorge Ranch and seven at the OC-6 takeout. We are extremely grateful for every one of them, but we still have 25 volunteer positions available at River Gorge Ranch. This will be an exciting and rewarding place to volunteer. You’ll be part of the inaugural Chattajack Village crew, first to welcome racers after their 31-mile journey through the Tennessee River Gorge and helping create the organized, encouraging and memorable experience they deserve. Volunteers will help set up and break down tents, organize resources, distribute finisher medals and nutrition, direct racers and their vessels, assist with shuttle loading, and keep everything flowing smoothly throughout the afternoon. There are roles for a variety of abilities, including positions that do not require heavy lifting. Thank you to the awesome folks who have already signed up as medical volunteers—you are critical to this event! We would love to add a few more, so if you possess medical training, please consider joining Amy Campbell’s amazing medical team. Opportunities are available aboard support boats and at the River Gorge Ranch takeout. This is the first year for Chattajack Village, and our volunteers will forever be the crew that helped launch it. We cannot do it without you! There's also always that nice CJ vol perk of: anyone who fulfills a Chattajack volunteer role in 2026 receives priority registration for the 2027 race. Come share the excitement, support our paddlers and help us create an unforgettable Chattajack experience! Sign up here: https://www.signupgenius.com/…/4090F48A4AD2EA7F58-65038929-…

The Tri-State Mutual Aid Association will host a two-day swiftwater rescue training event, bringing together regional emergency response teams to refine critical water rescue skills and enhance multi-agency coordination. The exercise on September 29-30, 2026 will take place on the Ocoee River. Hamilton County Special Tactics & Rescue Services (STARS), the Chattanooga Fire Department, and the Cleveland Fire Department are involved, in conjunction with Ocoee River State Park, TVA, and the US Forest Service.  Training evolutions will run throughout both days. Participating swiftwater rescue personnel will rotate through multiple high-intensity hands-on skills stations.  Training together on the water ensures swiftwater teams speak the same operational language, align safety protocols, and build the seamless trust required when combining forces during critical rescue operations. The Chattanooga Fire Fighters Association Local 820, Big Woody’s Tree Service, and Morning Pointe Senior Living have been strong supporters of this fantastic learning opportunity and we appreciate their partnership.

Critical services for survivors are at risk. Join advocates nationwide TODAY in urging Senate leadership to pass the bipartisan Crime Victims Fund Stabilization Act. The Crime Victims Fund supports services for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, child sexual abuse, trafficking, and other crimes. It is funded by monetary penalties from federal criminal cases, not taxpayer dollars.  But annual deposits have dropped by an average of $1.5 billion over the past decade, and the fund’s remaining buffer is gone. Programs are already reducing services, laying off staff, and closing their doors. The Stabilization Act would redirect unobligated funds from the False Claims Act into the CVF, helping preserve critical services without using taxpayer dollars. The House passed the bill unanimously. Now the Senate must act. Contact your U.S. senators TODAY. Survivors can’t afford to wait. #cvsa #LeaderJohnThune #SenSchumer #ChuckGrassley #SenatorDurbin #MarshaBlackburn #billhaggerty

Join the City of Chattanooga Team Chattanooga , a vibrant and growing community of over 190,000 residents within a metropolitan area of nearly 600,000 is known as the "Scenic City" for a reason. Nestled along the Tennessee River and surrounded by the foothills of the Appalachian Mountains, we are a hub of outdoor adventure and innovation. Home to the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga (UTC) and Chattanooga State Community College , our city blends a rich industrial history with a tech-forward future—famously powered by the nation’s first community-wide "Gig" fiber-optic network.​ The City of Chattanooga was also recently designated as a "National Park City,” the first of its kind in the United States. Our Organization As a City, we are powered by a dedicated workforce of approximately ​ 2,600 employees committed to excellence in public service and making Chattanooga the best community in the country. Our team ensures our city thrives through a wide range of municipal services, including: Public Safety: Chattanooga Police and Fire Departments. Infrastructure Utilities: Public Works, Waste Resources, and specialized Stormwater management. Quality of Life: Award-winning Parks and Outdoors and Community Development systems and the Chattanooga Public Library. Transportation: The Chattanooga Metropolitan Airport (CHA) and citywide transit and pedestrian friendly initiatives. Innovation: Leading-edge smart-city programs with a commitment to cutting edge workforce development policies to ensure all our residents can get ahead. Why Choose Chattanooga? The City of Chattanooga’s workforce is the heartbeat of our community. We don't just offer jobs; we offer careers with purpose: making Chattanooga the best city in America. We are committed to being the premier employer of choice in Southeast Tennessee by providing: Competitive Compensation: Robust pay scales that reflect our commitment to our staff. Work-Life Balance: Generous paid time off and flexible scheduling where possible. Exceptional Wellness: Comprehensive health benefits and wellness programs designed for you and your family that deliver savings to you beyond your paycheck, featuring a centralized health clinic and pharmacy for all City employees. . Growth: A focus on professional development and upward mobility within the organization. ​The Great Outdoors: Your Backyard Playground: Chattanooga isn't just near nature, it's immersed in it. As one of the most biodiverse cities in North America, the "Scenic City" offers an ecological richness that few places on earth can claim. Whether you are an adrenaline junkie or a weekend wanderer, world-class adventure is always less than an hour away. ​Vertical Adventures: Scale legendary sandstone cliffs in what is widely considered the premier rock climbing hub of the Southeast. Water Rapids: From the high-octane whitewater kayaking of the Ocoee River to world-class bass fishing and peaceful paddling on the Tennessee River. Trails for Miles: Explore a massive network of mountain biking and hiking trails that wind through lush ridges, hidden waterfalls, and deep river gorges. In Chattanooga, "work-life balance" means you can finish your shift and be at a trailhead or on the water before the sun sets. Our mission is to work together to build a safe, vibrant, and sustainable city for all Chattanoogans. To do that, it takes a team of skilled and passionate individuals. So, if you’d like to call Chattanooga home – or maybe you already do! – and want to further your career through meaningful work that makes a true impact where you live, we’d love to talk to you. ____________________________________________________________________________ Salary: GS.08 $22.74 - $24.87 per hour Work Hours: Monday - Friday, 7:00 A.M. - 3:30 P.M. Incumbent(s) may not be required to perform all duties listed and may be required to perform additional, position-specific duties.) Operates various equipment and vehicles to complete tasks related to the maintenance, upkeep, installation and construction of city grounds, property, utilities, rights-of-way, and other infrastructure for Public Works; drives vehicles over public roads, worksites, right-of-way, parks, public works facilities, and other city property; maneuvers in and around traffic, parked cars, equipment, utilities, and other obstacles; obeys all traffic laws and safety guidelines, monitors immediate environment and work are to ensure the safety of the operator, other workers, the equipment and the public. Some positions may drive tandem and tri-axle dump trucks to transport and haul materials between original and final destinations for use in maintenance and construction projects; positions vehicle to allow for the most efficient and effective loading or dumping of materials; secures all doors, gates, and fasteners to prevent spillage or loss of load; operates dumping mechanism to dump materials at appropriate locations. Operates mowing tractors with articulated boom mowing system to mow rights-of-way and other City property along steep slopes, ditches, and hard-to-reach areas inaccessible to most mowing apparatuses; scouts path for and removes rocks, debris and other obstacles that may cause damage to the equipment, property or the public; determines proper settings and adjusts boom for the proper angle, height, and trajectory; maneuvers and monitors boom mower for optimal operation. Drives low-boy and other tractor-trailer rigs to transport heavy construction equipment and materials to and from work-sites; maneuvers equipment to load and unload from the trailer, operating mechanisms as necessary to position for safe transportation. Drives a variety of garbage trucks along a prescribed commercial or residential route to collect refuse; makes frequent stops at appropriate intervals to position truck near refuse containers; retrieves refuse container and attaches to automated dumping mechanism; dumps refuse and returns container; maintains the pace of collection activities to ensure timely completion of the assigned route. Drives fuel truck to transport fuel to equipment at work sites; operates the mechanism to fuel equipment as necessary; applies knowledge of hazardous materials when transporting, handling, and responding to spills involving gasoline, diesel fuel, and other flammable/volatile liquids. Drives bucket and/or lift truck to work site and operates lift mechanisms to elevate crews performing various maintenance, upkeep and installation for traffic systems, tree trimming and other tasks requiring access to high places; positions vehicle and lift-platform to ensure optimum access to the required location and avoid power lines, low branches, traffic and other hazards; monitors activities to ensure the safety of crew workers. Operates a jet-flushing/vacuum/viewer truck for the purpose of cleaning out storm drain and sanitary sewer pipe, manholes, catch basins and other brick and concrete drainage structures in order to maintain the flow throughout the stormwater drainage and sewer waste systems. Drives trucks with a side-mounted articulated vacuum boom along an assigned route for the purpose of picking up leaves, litter, and other yard waste from rights-of-way and out of drainage measurements in order to maintain stormwater drainage flow throughout the entire system. Inspects and prepares equipment for safe and proper operation prior to beginning work for the day; performs light maintenance on equipment which includes refueling and refilling lubricants; cleans vehicles, beds, and mounted equipment upon completion of assignments; secures vehicle after use. Sanitize and clean assigned equipment daily. Performs basic and semi-skilled labor as appropriate to assist in the completion of maintenance, upkeep and construction projects; picks up paper, limbs and other debris; uses hand tools and operates motorized tools as necessary to complete the assigned task. May remove dead animals and trees from the right of way as well as public roads. May answer 911 emergency calls for oil spills as well as black ice. May assist in contacting departments or personnel for an emergency situation. May be required to use, carry and answer cell phones, other devices, and/or two-way radio as determined by their job duties and their supervisor. Must meet regular attendance requirements. Must be able to maintain good interpersonal relationships with staff, co-workers, managers and citizens. Must accomplish the essential functions of the job, with or without reasonable accommodations, in a timely manner. May be assigned or reassigned to any division within the department. Performs other related duties as required. This position is deemed essential during inclement weather situations, and must report to or remain at work, even when administrative closings are announced, as determined by the Department Head. DEPARTMENT SPECIFIC DUTIES: When working in Forestry division: Uses of chainsaws, rigging lines, pulleys, and cranes. Working in high traffic areas with the use of signs, cones, and flaggers and in the vicinity of power lines, moving traffic or directly above buildings. Removes and cleans up dead or hazardous trees. Available on call for storm work or downed trees. May train personnel. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: High School Diploma or GED and one (1) year of any combination of relevant education, experience, and/or training sufficient to successfully perform the essential functions of this job; or any combination of equivalent experience and education. Bucket Truck experience strongly preferred. LICENSING AND CERTIFICATIONS: Valid Class A, Class A restricted or Class B commercial driver license. Requires appropriate license endorsement(s) related to the area of assignment. KNOWLEDGE SKILLS: Knowledge of occupational hazards and safety precautions; general equipment and maintenance principles; materials and equipment utilized in assigned area of responsibility; demonstrated ability to drive and operate assigned equipment; operation of commercial vehicles that consist of self-contained specialized equipment. Typical equipment operated might include, but is not limited to: tractor-trailers, low boys, fuel trucks, bucket trucks, mechanical street sweepers, knuckle-boom trucks, articulated boom mowers, oil distributors, jet-flushing/vacuum trucks, CCTV equipped trucks and automated garbage trucks with an articulated arm. Must be able to use electronic devices to receive and track work. The position requires minimal, but daily public interaction and must be customer service centered, focused, and able to recognize or resolve customer needs according to departmental practices. PHYSICAL DEMANDS: Positions in this class typically require climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, crawling, reaching, standing, walking, pushing, pulling, lifting, fingering, grasping, feeling, talking, hearing, seeing and repetitive motions. WORK ENVIRONMENT: Medium Work: Exerting up-to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up-to 20 pounds of force frequently, and/or up-to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects. SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: Safety Sensitive: Y Department of Transportation - CDL: Y Child Sensitive: N SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION: This position requires pre-employment screening(s) that include: background check / drug screening / lift test / DOT Clearinghouse The City of Chattanooga, Tennessee is an Equal Opportunity Employer. In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, the City will provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities and encourage both prospective and current employees to discuss potential accommodations with the employer. A broken thermometer at a Chattanooga school resulted in a hazmat response and multiple people being transported to the hospital Wednesday morning. On 9/23/26, Blue Shift companies responded to Dalewood Middle School at 1300 Shallowford Road after students and teachers were possibly exposed to mercury.  A thermometer was dropped during a routine experiment in a science lab. At first, it was suspected of containing mercury. It has now been determined that the thermometer was alcohol based and there was no harm to students or staff.  Officials treated the incident as a possible mercury exposure until the substance could be identified by an environmental company.  Fourteen students were transported by ambulance or personal vehicle to the hospital. Two teachers were also transported. They were taken to the hospital as a precautionary measure. The heating and air conditioning was shut down to the building and the rest of the student body was dismissed. Marion Environmental responded to the school to handle the remediation and confirmed that it was an alcohol thermometer. No mercury was involved.  CFD Hazmat 1, Special Operations, Squad 1, Engine 15, and members of the command staff responded to Dalewood Middle, in addition to CPD, Hamilton County EMS and officials with Hamilton County Schools.

Join the City of Chattanooga Team Chattanooga , a vibrant and growing community of over 190,000 residents within a metropolitan area of nearly 600,000 is known as the "Scenic City" for a reason. Nestled along the Tennessee River and surrounded by the foothills of the Appalachian Mountains, we are a hub of outdoor adventure and innovation. Home to the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga (UTC) and Chattanooga State Community College , our city blends a rich industrial history with a tech-forward future—famously powered by the nation’s first community-wide "Gig" fiber-optic network.​ The City of Chattanooga was also recently designated as a "National Park City,” the first of its kind in the United States. Our Organization As a City, we are powered by a dedicated workforce of approximately ​ 2,600 employees committed to excellence in public service and making Chattanooga the best community in the country. Our team ensures our city thrives through a wide range of municipal services, including: Public Safety: Chattanooga Police and Fire Departments. Infrastructure Utilities: Public Works, Waste Resources, and specialized Stormwater management. Quality of Life: Award-winning Parks and Outdoors and Community Development systems and the Chattanooga Public Library. Transportation: The Chattanooga Metropolitan Airport (CHA) and citywide transit and pedestrian friendly initiatives. Innovation: Leading-edge smart-city programs with a commitment to cutting edge workforce development policies to ensure all our residents can get ahead. Why Choose Chattanooga? The City of Chattanooga’s workforce is the heartbeat of our community. We don't just offer jobs; we offer careers with purpose: making Chattanooga the best city in America. We are committed to being the premier employer of choice in Southeast Tennessee by providing: Competitive Compensation: Robust pay scales that reflect our commitment to our staff. Work-Life Balance: Generous paid time off and flexible scheduling where possible. Exceptional Wellness: Comprehensive health benefits and wellness programs designed for you and your family that deliver savings to you beyond your paycheck, featuring a centralized health clinic and pharmacy for all City employees. . Growth: A focus on professional development and upward mobility within the organization. ​The Great Outdoors: Your Backyard Playground: Chattanooga isn't just near nature, it's immersed in it. As one of the most biodiverse cities in North America, the "Scenic City" offers an ecological richness that few places on earth can claim. Whether you are an adrenaline junkie or a weekend wanderer, world-class adventure is always less than an hour away. ​Vertical Adventures: Scale legendary sandstone cliffs in what is widely considered the premier rock climbing hub of the Southeast. Water Rapids: From the high-octane whitewater kayaking of the Ocoee River to world-class bass fishing and peaceful paddling on the Tennessee River. Trails for Miles: Explore a massive network of mountain biking and hiking trails that wind through lush ridges, hidden waterfalls, and deep river gorges. In Chattanooga, "work-life balance" means you can finish your shift and be at a trailhead or on the water before the sun sets. CPD Investigating Deadly Crash Involving a Pedestrian on Shallowford Road CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. -- The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) is investigating a crash that resulted in a pedestrian's death Monday afternoon. At approximately 11:00 a.m., CPD's Traffic Unit responded to a crash involving a pedestrian in the 7500 block of Shallowford Road. Preliminary findings indicate the pedestrian, a 65-year-old woman, was attempting to cross the road and stepped in front of a vehicle. The driver attempted to swerve, but still hit the pedestrian. Hamilton County EMS responded and transported the woman to the hospital where she was pronounced dead.  This information is preliminary and subject to change as the investigation continues. Chattanooga Police ask anyone with information regarding this incident to call 423-698-2525. #CPDnews

Before you decide mountain biking "isn't for you," we need to clear a few things up. 👀🚲 You do NOT need your own mountain bike. You do NOT need experience. Field FUNdamentals starts with the basics in a controlled environment at Greenway Farm, where you can practice things like braking, shifting, balance, body position and bike control before ever taking those skills onto a trail. Bike and helmet reservations are available, classes are just $10, and beginners are very much invited. All you really need is a pair of closed-toed shoes and a willingness to try something new. 🗓Tuesdays through November 3 📍Greenway Farm 🎟Register at outdoorchattanooga.com/calendar Come see what all the mountain biking hype is about!

A yacht was destroyed by fire Wednesday afternoon in Downtown Chattanooga. At 1:03 PM on 9/16/26, Red Shift companies were dispatched to 419 Riverfront Parkway near Scottie’s on The River Restaurant.  Firefighters made their way down to the dock with more than 600 feet of fire hose and tackled the blaze, supported by our fire boats drafting water from the Tennessee River. It appears that the vessels on either side of the burning boat sustained some radiant heat damage, but firefighters did an excellent job protecting those exposures.  River boom materials were placed around the boat to contain any fuel leaks. The cause of the fire is under investigation. There were no injuries.  Squad 1, Ladder 1, Fireboat 10, Fireboat 6, Engine 12, Battalion 1, CFD Special Operations, CFD Safety, CFD Supply, and CFD’s Training Chief were on the scene.

Greenway Farm Garden Project.  Looking fantastic at Greenway Farm.  In 1988, a few local gardeners asked Dr. Spangler if they could plant a garden on his 160-acre farmland—what is now Greenway Farm Park. Delighted by the idea, he had his caretaker plow a plot so Hixson-area residents could grow their own food. In 1990, the City of Chattanooga purchased the land, and the Greenway Farm Gardeners continued under the North Chickamauga Conservatory. In 2025, they became an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit: the Greenway Farm Garden Project. Thanks to a lease with the City of Chattanooga Parks and Outdoors, their mission continues. The gardeners come from all around and share a passion for growing, teaching, and preserving both Greenway Farm Park and traditional gardening practices for future generations. Free educational sessions are offered on the second Saturday of every month from 10:00–11:00 AM, right next to the gardens. Visitors are welcome to stop by anytime, introduce themselves to the gardeners (who are happy to show people around), or contact the president, Sheri Steele, at sheristeele2020@gmail.com for open plots and information.   *Note their next class is Oct 10th focusing on winter prep for gardens*

It’s a model project for excellence for other designs like it at other parks and playgrounds!

Join the City of Chattanooga Team Chattanooga , a vibrant and growing community of over 190,000 residents within a metropolitan area of nearly 600,000 is known as the "Scenic City" for a reason. Nestled along the Tennessee River and surrounded by the foothills of the Appalachian Mountains, we are a hub of outdoor adventure and innovation. Home to the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga (UTC) and Chattanooga State Community College , our city blends a rich industrial history with a tech-forward future—famously powered by the nation’s first community-wide "Gig" fiber-optic network.​ The City of Chattanooga was also recently designated as a "National Park City,” the first of its kind in the United States. Our Organization As a City, we are powered by a dedicated workforce of approximately ​ 2,600 employees committed to excellence in public service and making Chattanooga the best community in the country. Our team ensures our city thrives through a wide range of municipal services, including: Public Safety: Chattanooga Police and Fire Departments. Infrastructure Utilities: Public Works, Waste Resources, and specialized Stormwater management. Quality of Life: Award-winning Parks and Outdoors and Community Development systems and the Chattanooga Public Library. Transportation: The Chattanooga Metropolitan Airport (CHA) and citywide transit and pedestrian friendly initiatives. Innovation: Leading-edge smart-city programs with a commitment to cutting edge workforce development policies to ensure all our residents can get ahead. Why Choose Chattanooga? The City of Chattanooga’s workforce is the heartbeat of our community. We don't just offer jobs; we offer careers with purpose: making Chattanooga the best city in America. We are committed to being the premier employer of choice in Southeast Tennessee by providing: Competitive Compensation: Robust pay scales that reflect our commitment to our staff. Work-Life Balance: Generous paid time off and flexible scheduling where possible. Exceptional Wellness: Comprehensive health benefits and wellness programs designed for you and your family that deliver savings to you beyond your paycheck, featuring a centralized health clinic and pharmacy for all City employees. . Growth: A focus on professional development and upward mobility within the organization. ​The Great Outdoors: Your Backyard Playground: Chattanooga isn't just near nature, it's immersed in it. As one of the most biodiverse cities in North America, the "Scenic City" offers an ecological richness that few places on earth can claim. Whether you are an adrenaline junkie or a weekend wanderer, world-class adventure is always less than an hour away. ​Vertical Adventures: Scale legendary sandstone cliffs in what is widely considered the premier rock climbing hub of the Southeast. Water Rapids: From the high-octane whitewater kayaking of the Ocoee River to world-class bass fishing and peaceful paddling on the Tennessee River. Trails for Miles: Explore a massive network of mountain biking and hiking trails that wind through lush ridges, hidden waterfalls, and deep river gorges. In Chattanooga, "work-life balance" means you can finish your shift and be at a trailhead or on the water before the sun sets.
